gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-anek-telugu: Anek Telugu reads with wide, tall bowls that keep their rounds unlatched, a friendly rhythm from line to line. Edo SZ earns its place big and brief, where its constant-width lines and cast-iron stature can stand alone.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-anuphan: Classic in feeling, Edo SZ draws its lowercase tall as cast iron capitals, with no pinched joins or swelling bowls. And Anuphan, a sans-serif, does the quieter work, with big round bowls and open curves that leave clear gaps.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-arimo: Cultural in its bearing, Edo SZ lays fine-rope strokes into letter shapes and lets that single line width carry the weight. Then Arimo, a sans-serif, takes over the steady work with its tall mean line and spacious gaps in the rounds.

gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-atkinson-hyperlegib: Approachable in its feel, Atkinson Hyperlegible keeps wide-set terminals on s, though its capitals and ascenders look clipped beside the lowercase.
